2609.15106.title: When the Wrong Key Wins: Understanding and Detecting Hallucinations in LLMs
2609.15106.paper_summary: Large language models can hallucinate even when the knowledge required for a correct answer is already available. We study this failure through a latent-key view of inference, where answer selection depends on competition among associations acquired during pretraining. We show that model predictions can be highly sensitive to individual query keywords, that these influential keywords exhibit entity-specific binding, and that their effects are systematically shaped by pretraining frequency. Multiple bindings can also compete and exhibit higher-order interactions within the same query. Based on this mechanism, we introduce a two-stage keyword-perturbation method for hallucination detection. By removing influential keywords and measuring how the model reorganizes its prediction, the method distinguishes errors caused by misleading key associations from correct decisions supported by diagnostic evidence. Across multiple models and benchmarks, perturbation provides a strong and transferable detection signal, reaching $.910$ AUROC on probe-known ScientistQA. Finally, we extend the same probabilistic framework to four hallucination regimes: knowledge deficit, wrong knowledge, context distraction, and unstable inference. Their operational distributions across benchmarks provide diagnostic context for why different detector families succeed in different settings.
2609.15106.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型即使在正確答案所需的知識已經可用的情況下仍然會出現幻覺。我們通過潛在關鍵視角來研究這種失敗，在這種視角下，答案的選擇依賴於在預訓練期間獲得的聯想之間的競爭。我們顯示模型預測對個別查詢關鍵字的敏感性很高，這些有影響力的關鍵字表現出特定實體的綁定，其影響受到預訓練頻率的系統性塑造。多重綁定也可以在同一查詢中競爭並表現出高階交互。基於這一機制，我們引入了一種兩階段的關鍵字擾動方法來檢測幻覺。通過去除有影響力的關鍵字並測量模型如何重新組織其預測，該方法區分了由誤導性關鍵聯想引起的錯誤與由診斷證據支持的正確決策。在多個模型和基準測試中，擾動提供了一個強大且可轉移的檢測信號，在 probe-known ScientistQA 上達到 $.910$ AUROC。最後，我們將相同的概率框架擴展到四種幻覺範疇：知識缺失、錯誤知識、上下文干擾和不穩定推理。它們在基準測試中的操作分佈提供了診斷背景，解釋為什麼不同的檢測器家族在不同的設置中成功。
2609.15106.author: Xuhan Tong et.al.
